data.notes_riya: both are food but not same type of food; wendy's is a restaurant while this company sells packaged food. In addition, the customer groups are different
data.notes_barbara:
Different products; Different customers; Different business model

Hormel sells packaged foods to retail and foodservice buyers. It is a food manufacturer rather than a restaurant operator.
data.notes_matthew: Hormel is packaged meat. About a third of its sales go to foodservice, which again makes it a supplier to restaurants rather than a peer.

data.reason: Wendy's runs and franchises quick-service hamburger restaurants that serve prepared food to consumers at drive-thrus, in stores and by delivery. Hormel makes and brands packaged foods and sells them to grocers and foodservice buyers. The two don't overlap in product, customer or how they earn money.
Different business model: Hormel sells branded food products in stores and foodservice channels rather than operating a prepared-meal restaurant offering.
